questions.topic: History of Community Health Nursing in Ghana
questions.question_text: What is the primary purpose of Community Health Nursing?

choices.text: To provide health services exclusively to patients admitted to hospitals
To promote, protect and maintain the health of individuals, families and communities
To provide specialist surgical services in urban hospitals
To focus only on the treatment of communicable diseases

questions.rationale: Community Health Nursing emphasizes health promotion, disease prevention, early identification of health problems and appropriate care within communities. Its activities address individuals, families and populations rather than focusing exclusively on institutional treatment.

questions.topic: History of Community Health Nursing in Ghana
questions.question_text: Which Ghanaian initiative is widely associated with the development and expansion of community-based primary healthcare delivery?

choices.text: National Health Insurance Scheme
Community-based Health Planning and Services (CHPS)
National Ambulance Service
National Blood Service

questions.rationale: CHPS was developed to bring essential primary healthcare services closer to households through community-based service delivery. Its development was informed by community health research and operational experience, including the Navrongo experiment. Ghana Health Service

questions.topic: History of Community Health Nursing in Ghana
questions.question_text: The Navrongo Community Health and Family Planning Project, which contributed to the development of CHPS, was launched as an operations research project in which year?
questions.rationale: The Navrongo experiment began in 1994 and examined different approaches to delivering community-based health and family planning services. Its findings contributed to the development of Ghana's CHPS strategy. Ghana Health Service

questions.topic: N&MC Regulations and Scope of Practice
questions.question_text: What is the primary statutory purpose of the Nursing and Midwifery Council of Ghana?

choices.text: To manage all public hospitals in Ghana
To secure the highest standards of nursing and midwifery training and practice in the public interest
To determine the salaries of all healthcare workers
To provide financial assistance to every nursing student

questions.rationale: The Nursing and Midwifery Council of Ghana is a statutory regulatory body established under the Health Professions Regulatory Bodies Act, 2013 (Act 857). Its mandate includes regulating professional education, registration, licensing, standards and conduct. NMC Ghana

questions.topic: N&MC Regulations and Scope of Practice
questions.question_text: Which legislation established the current statutory framework for the Nursing and Midwifery Council of Ghana?

choices.text: Health Professions Regulatory Bodies Act, 2013 (Act 857)
Public Health Act, 2012 (Act 851)
Children's Act, 1998 (Act 560)
National Health Insurance Act, 2012 (Act 852)

questions.rationale: The Health Professions Regulatory Bodies Act, 2013 (Act 857) provides the statutory framework for the Nursing and Midwifery Council. It establishes the Council's regulatory mandate over nursing and midwifery education and professional practice. NMC Ghana

questions.topic: N&MC Regulations and Scope of Practice
questions.question_text: Which statement best defines the professional scope of practice of a Community Health Nurse?

choices.text: All activities that a nurse personally prefers to perform
The roles and activities the nurse is educated, competent and authorized to perform
Any procedure requested by a community member
Only duties assigned by a traditional community leader

questions.rationale: Scope of practice defines the professional roles and activities a nurse is qualified and authorized to perform. A nurse must work within the limits of education, competence, applicable regulations and approved clinical protocols. NMC Ghana

questions.topic: Professional Ethics and Code of Conduct
questions.question_text: Which ethical principle requires a Community Health Nurse to respect a client's right to make decisions about personal healthcare?

choices.text: Autonomy
Justice
Beneficence
Non-maleficence

questions.rationale: Autonomy recognizes an individual's right to make informed decisions about personal healthcare. The nurse should provide relevant information, respect the client's choices and avoid coercion.

questions.topic: Professional Ethics and Code of Conduct
questions.question_text: Which ethical principle means that a nurse should act to promote the wellbeing of clients?

choices.text: Fidelity
Beneficence
Confidentiality
Veracity

questions.rationale: Beneficence is the ethical obligation to act for the benefit and wellbeing of clients. Community Health Nurses demonstrate this principle through appropriate health education, preventive interventions and patient-centred care.

questions.topic: Professional Ethics and Code of Conduct
questions.question_text: What does the ethical principle of non-maleficence require of a Community Health Nurse?

choices.text: To provide services only to clients who can pay
To avoid causing preventable harm to clients
To disclose all client information to community leaders
To allow clients to determine the nurse's professional duties

questions.rationale: Non-maleficence means avoiding or minimizing harm. Nurses apply this principle by practising competently, following safety procedures and referring clients when their needs exceed the nurse's competence.

questions.topic: Patient Rights and Advocacy
questions.question_text: Which of the following is a fundamental right of a person receiving healthcare?

choices.text: The right to demand any treatment regardless of clinical appropriateness
The right to receive respectful care and understandable information
The right to access another patient's medical records
The right to prevent healthcare workers from documenting care

questions.rationale: Patients are entitled to dignity, respectful treatment and information that supports informed decision-making. These rights must be balanced with applicable laws, clinical standards and the rights of others.

questions.topic: Legal Issues in Community Nursing
questions.question_text: In nursing practice, what is negligence?

choices.text: A deliberate decision to promote a client's independence
Failure to exercise the reasonable standard of care expected, resulting in harm or risk of harm
The appropriate referral of a client to a higher-level facility
The provision of health education during a home visit

questions.rationale: Negligence involves a failure to meet the required standard of reasonable care. In a legal claim, relevant issues generally include a duty of care, breach, causation and legally recognizable damage.

questions.topic: Legal Issues in Community Nursing
questions.question_text: What is informed consent?

choices.text: Permission obtained after a client receives relevant information and understands the proposed intervention
Permission obtained from a relative for every adult client
A nurse's decision to proceed without explaining a procedure
A general agreement to receive all future treatments

questions.rationale: Informed consent requires adequate information, understanding and a voluntary decision by a person with decision-making capacity. The information should include the nature, benefits, material risks and reasonable alternatives to the proposed intervention.

questions.topic: Professional Boundaries
questions.question_text: What are professional boundaries in Community Health Nursing?

choices.text: Rules that prevent nurses from communicating with clients
Limits that maintain a safe, respectful and professional nurse-client relationship
Restrictions that allow nurses to ignore community concerns
Personal rules that clients must follow outside healthcare settings

questions.rationale: Professional boundaries define appropriate limits within the nurse-client relationship. They protect clients from exploitation and help maintain trust, objectivity and professional accountability.

questions.topic: Community Health Nursing as a Profession
questions.question_text: Which characteristic distinguishes nursing as a profession?

choices.text: Practice based entirely on personal opinion
Specialized knowledge, regulated practice, ethical standards and professional accountability
Absence of formal education and professional supervision
Freedom to perform any clinical procedure without authorization

questions.rationale: Nursing is a profession because it requires specialized education, defined competencies, ethical standards and accountability to a regulatory body. Professional practice also involves continuing development and evidence-based care.

questions.topic: Communication and Documentation Standards
questions.question_text: Which statement best describes accurate nursing documentation?

choices.text: Recording only unusual events at the end of the month
Making timely, factual, complete and legible records of care provided
Recording personal opinions as confirmed clinical findings
Allowing another person to document care that was not observed or verified

questions.rationale: Accurate documentation provides a reliable account of assessment, decisions, interventions and outcomes. It supports continuity of care, professional accountability and communication among healthcare providers.

questions.topic: Health Care Delivery System in Ghana and CHPS
questions.question_text: What is the central aim of the Community-based Health Planning and Services (CHPS) strategy in Ghana?

choices.text: To replace all district hospitals with community clinics
To bring essential primary healthcare services closer to communities through community participation
To provide specialist surgery in every community
To restrict healthcare delivery to people registered with NHIS

questions.rationale: CHPS is designed to improve access to essential primary healthcare by delivering services close to where people live. Community participation, household engagement and collaboration with local structures are important elements of the strategy. Ministry Of Health

questions.topic: History of Community Health Nursing in Ghana
questions.question_text: A Community Health Nurse is assigned to a rural CHPS zone where many children have incomplete immunization. Which professional role is most appropriate?

choices.text: Wait for parents to bring every child to the district hospital
Identify under-immunized children, engage caregivers and organize appropriate immunization follow-up
Stop immunization activities until every household requests them
Refer all children to a specialist hospital without assessment

questions.rationale: Community Health Nurses support immunization through outreach, caregiver education, follow-up and appropriate documentation. Identifying children who have missed scheduled vaccines helps improve coverage and prevent vaccine-preventable diseases.

questions.topic: N&MC Regulations and Scope of Practice
questions.question_text: A Community Health Nurse is asked by a community leader to perform a clinical procedure for which the nurse has not been trained or authorized. What should the nurse do?

choices.text: Perform the procedure because the community leader has requested it
Politely explain the limitation, seek assistance from a competent practitioner and arrange appropriate referral
Attempt the procedure after reading a short online description
Ask an untrained volunteer to perform the procedure

questions.rationale: A nurse must practise within the limits of competence and authorized scope of practice. When a client's needs exceed those limits, the nurse should obtain appropriate assistance or arrange referral rather than undertaking an unsafe intervention.

questions.topic: N&MC Regulations and Scope of Practice
questions.question_text: A newly posted Community Health Nurse is unsure whether a particular intervention is within the nurse's authorized scope of practice. What is the most appropriate action?

choices.text: Proceed because all nurses have identical authority to perform every procedure
Consult the applicable N&MC scope of practice, facility protocols and an appropriate supervisor before proceeding
Ask a community volunteer to decide whether the procedure is permitted
Perform the procedure first and seek approval afterwards

questions.rationale: The N&MC scope of practice and applicable approved protocols guide professional responsibilities. Clarifying uncertainty before acting helps prevent unsafe practice and protects the nurse and client.

questions.topic: Professional Ethics and Code of Conduct
questions.question_text: During a home visit, a nurse discovers that a client cannot afford the prescribed treatment. Which action best demonstrates professional ethics?

choices.text: Refuse to assess the client because payment is not available
Assess the client's needs, explain available care options and facilitate appropriate support or referral
Publicly announce the client's financial difficulties
Advise the client to use another person's medication

questions.rationale: Ethical nursing practice requires fairness, respect and attention to barriers that affect access to care. The nurse should explore appropriate service options and referrals without compromising safety or confidentiality.

questions.topic: Professional Ethics and Code of Conduct
questions.question_text: A nurse receives money from a client in exchange for placing the client's name ahead of others on a routine clinic list. Which professional obligation has been violated?

choices.text: Professional integrity and fairness
Continuing professional development
Community participation
Health education

questions.rationale: Accepting payment to provide unfair preferential treatment is an abuse of professional position. Nurses must act honestly, avoid improper personal gain and treat clients fairly according to legitimate clinical and service priorities.

questions.topic: Patient Rights and Advocacy
questions.question_text: A competent adult client refuses a recommended screening test after the nurse has explained its purpose and possible consequences. What should the nurse do?

choices.text: Force the client to undergo the test
Respect the informed refusal, explore the client's concerns and document the discussion
Threaten to withdraw all future healthcare
Ask a relative to consent without the client's permission

questions.rationale: A competent adult has the right to make informed decisions, including refusing a proposed intervention. The nurse should ensure the client understands the relevant information, document the decision and continue appropriate care.

questions.topic: Patient Rights and Advocacy
questions.question_text: A client complains that a health worker spoke disrespectfully to her during a clinic visit. What is the most appropriate response by the Community Health Nurse receiving the complaint?

choices.text: Tell the client that health workers cannot be questioned
Listen respectfully, clarify the complaint and explain the appropriate complaint or reporting process
Dismiss the complaint because no physical injury occurred
Share the complaint with other clients for discussion

questions.rationale: Patient advocacy includes listening to concerns and supporting clients to raise complaints through appropriate channels. Respectful handling of complaints promotes accountability and helps improve the quality of healthcare services.

questions.topic: Legal Issues in Community Nursing
questions.question_text: A nurse administers a medication without checking the client's identity and gives it to the wrong person. What should the nurse do FIRST after recognizing the error?

choices.text: Alter the documentation to conceal the mistake
Assess the affected client immediately, seek appropriate clinical assistance and report the incident through the required procedure
Wait until the client develops symptoms before taking action
Blame the person who prepared the medication

questions.rationale: The immediate priority after a medication error is to assess and protect the affected client. The nurse must obtain appropriate clinical support, report the incident honestly and complete accurate documentation according to facility policy.

questions.topic: Legal Issues in Community Nursing
questions.question_text: During a home visit, a nurse explains a proposed wound dressing procedure, its purpose and possible discomfort. The client understands and agrees. What should the nurse do before proceeding?

choices.text: Obtain and document the client's consent according to applicable procedure and policy
Seek permission from the client's neighbour
Proceed without consent because the procedure is routine
Ask the client to sign a blank consent form

questions.rationale: Consent should be obtained before providing care that requires the client's permission. The client should have sufficient information and freedom to accept or refuse the procedure.

questions.topic: Professional Boundaries
questions.question_text: A Community Health Nurse is providing care to a client who offers an expensive personal gift in appreciation. What is the most appropriate action?

choices.text: Accept the gift and promise preferential treatment
Politely decline or follow the facility's gift policy and maintain professional boundaries
Accept the gift in exchange for the client's confidential information
Ask the client to provide gifts to other nurses as well

questions.rationale: Expensive gifts may create conflicts of interest, expectations of preferential treatment or inappropriate dependency. The nurse should follow professional and institutional guidance to preserve an objective therapeutic relationship.

questions.topic: Professional Boundaries
questions.question_text: A nurse begins a romantic relationship with a current client receiving regular care at a CHPS compound. Which statement best describes this situation?

choices.text: It is acceptable if the client initiates the relationship
It breaches professional boundaries because of the nurse's position of trust and the therapeutic relationship
It is acceptable if the nurse does not document the relationship
It is acceptable if other community members approve

questions.rationale: A nurse-client relationship involves a professional responsibility and an inherent power imbalance. Romantic or sexual involvement with a current client is incompatible with maintaining appropriate professional boundaries.

questions.topic: Community Health Nursing as a Profession
questions.question_text: A Community Health Nurse attends a professional workshop to update knowledge about childhood immunization. Which professional responsibility is being demonstrated?

choices.text: Professional misconduct
Continuing professional development
Unauthorized delegation
Breach of confidentiality

questions.rationale: Continuing professional development enables nurses to maintain and improve knowledge, skills and professional competence. It supports safe, evidence-based practice as healthcare needs and guidelines change.

questions.topic: Community Health Nursing as a Profession
questions.question_text: A nurse notices that a colleague repeatedly fails to follow infection prevention procedures during wound care. What is the most appropriate professional response?

choices.text: Ignore the practice because the colleague is experienced
Address the immediate safety risk, remind the colleague of the required standards and report persistent concerns through appropriate channels
Discuss the colleague's conduct publicly with community members
Copy the unsafe practice to avoid conflict

questions.rationale: Nurses share responsibility for maintaining patient safety and professional standards. Immediate risks should be addressed, and persistent unsafe practice should be escalated through appropriate supervisory or reporting procedures.

questions.topic: Communication and Documentation Standards
questions.question_text: During a home visit, a nurse finds that a child has a high temperature and poor feeding. Which documentation practice is most appropriate?

choices.text: Record only that the child was unwell
Document the assessment findings, relevant observations, advice, interventions, referrals and follow-up plan accurately
Record the findings several weeks later from memory
Document only the advice given to the caregiver

questions.rationale: Complete documentation should capture relevant findings, actions and plans in a timely manner. This information supports continuity of care, referral communication and accountability.

questions.topic: Communication and Documentation Standards
questions.question_text: A nurse realizes that an entry in a client's paper record contains an incorrect date. What is the appropriate way to correct the error?

choices.text: Erase the original entry completely so that no correction is visible
Correct it according to facility policy while preserving the original entry, and authenticate the correction
Ask another person to rewrite the entire record without explanation
Use correction fluid to cover the incorrect date

questions.rationale: Corrections to clinical records must preserve the integrity and traceability of the original documentation. The nurse should follow the approved record-correction procedure and authenticate the amendment.

questions.topic: Health Care Delivery System in Ghana and CHPS
questions.question_text: A nurse is posted to a new CHPS zone and wants to begin providing effective community services. What should the nurse do before planning major health interventions?

choices.text: Introduce services without consulting community members
Conduct community entry, engage local stakeholders and assess the community's health needs
Focus only on households that are close to the CHPS compound
Wait for the district hospital to identify every health problem

questions.rationale: Community entry helps the nurse establish trust and build relationships with community leaders and residents. A community assessment then provides information for planning relevant and acceptable health interventions.

questions.topic: Health Care Delivery System in Ghana and CHPS
questions.question_text: During community entry, a nurse is preparing to introduce a new health education programme. Which action is most appropriate?

choices.text: Meet relevant community leaders, explain the programme and encourage participation
Begin activities without informing the community
Ask only one household to determine the needs of the entire community
Require residents to participate before explaining the programme

questions.rationale: Engagement with community leaders and residents promotes trust, cooperation and local ownership. Explaining the purpose of the programme allows community members to contribute to planning and implementation.

questions.topic: Health Care Delivery System in Ghana and CHPS
questions.question_text: A client at a CHPS compound presents with severe difficulty in breathing and low oxygen saturation. The condition is beyond the facility's available management capacity. What should the Community Health Nurse do FIRST?

choices.text: Advise the client to return home and rest
Provide appropriate immediate care within competence, arrange urgent referral and communicate with the receiving facility
Wait until the next routine clinic session
Ask the client to find transport without providing assistance

questions.rationale: Severe respiratory distress is a potentially life-threatening emergency requiring prompt assessment and stabilization. The nurse should provide appropriate care within competence and arrange urgent transfer to a facility with the required resources.

questions.topic: Health Care Delivery System in Ghana and CHPS
questions.question_text: A community member complains that the CHPS compound is too far from several households. Which action best reflects the community-oriented role of the nurse?

choices.text: Dismiss the complaint because the facility location cannot be discussed
Discuss access barriers with community members and stakeholders and explore appropriate outreach or service-delivery arrangements
Stop providing services to households far from the compound
Advise all residents to relocate closer to the facility

questions.rationale: Community Health Nursing seeks to improve equitable access to essential services. Working with local stakeholders to identify barriers and plan appropriate outreach can help address geographical and practical difficulties.

questions.topic: Patient Rights and Advocacy
questions.question_text: A client tells a nurse that she cannot afford transport to attend a scheduled follow-up appointment. What should the nurse do?

choices.text: Remove the client from the follow-up register
Explore the barrier and discuss feasible follow-up arrangements or available community support
Tell the client that follow-up is not important
Record that the client is unwilling to receive care

questions.rationale: Patient advocacy includes identifying barriers that prevent access to essential healthcare. The nurse should explore practical solutions, such as appropriate community follow-up, while maintaining continuity and safety of care.

questions.topic: Professional Ethics and Code of Conduct
questions.question_text: A nurse discovers that a colleague has disclosed a client's HIV status to community members without authorization. What should the nurse do?

choices.text: Share the information with more people to confirm whether it is true
Protect the client's privacy, support the client and report the breach through the appropriate professional and institutional process
Ignore the incident because the information is already public
Post a warning about the client on a community noticeboard

questions.rationale: A client's HIV status is confidential health information and should not be disclosed without lawful justification or appropriate consent. The nurse should protect the client and follow the facility's incident-reporting and confidentiality procedures.

questions.topic: Legal Issues in Community Nursing
questions.question_text: A Community Health Nurse observes signs suggesting that a child may be experiencing physical abuse. What should the nurse do?

choices.text: Ignore the findings unless the child makes a formal written complaint
Assess immediate safety, document objective findings and follow applicable child-protection reporting and referral procedures
Confront the suspected person publicly before assessing the child
Promise the child that the information will never be shared with anyone

questions.rationale: Suspected child abuse requires a safety-focused and appropriately documented response. The nurse should follow Ghana's child-protection framework and relevant reporting and referral procedures rather than attempting to investigate or resolve the matter independently.

questions.topic: N&MC Regulations and Scope of Practice
questions.question_text: A Community Health Nurse delegates a routine task to a trained assistant. Which action remains the nurse's professional responsibility?

choices.text: Assuming that delegation transfers all accountability to the assistant
Ensuring that the task is appropriate, the assistant is competent and the required supervision is provided
Allowing the assistant to independently change the clinical plan
Avoiding follow-up because the task has been delegated

questions.rationale: Delegation requires the nurse to consider the task, the competence of the person receiving it and the level of supervision needed. Delegation does not remove the nurse's responsibility to ensure safe and appropriate care.

questions.topic: Communication and Documentation Standards
questions.question_text: A nurse refers a child with severe dehydration from a CHPS compound to a district hospital. Which information is most important to include in the referral communication?

choices.text: The nurse's personal opinion about the child's family
The child's identification, assessment findings, relevant treatment given, response and reason for referral
Only the name of the CHPS compound
Unrelated information about other children in the community

questions.rationale: A referral should communicate the clinical information needed for safe continuation of care. Relevant assessment findings, interventions and the reason for transfer help the receiving team make timely decisions.

questions.topic: Professional Boundaries
questions.question_text: A nurse is asked by a client's family to disclose the client's diagnosis, but the client has not authorized the disclosure. What should the nurse do?

choices.text: Disclose the diagnosis because relatives are automatically entitled to all health information
Maintain confidentiality and seek the client's consent before sharing information, unless a lawful exception applies
Give the family a copy of the entire medical record
Discuss the diagnosis with neighbours instead

questions.rationale: Confidentiality requires nurses to protect personal health information from unauthorized disclosure. Information may be shared with family members when the client consents or when a lawful and appropriate exception applies.

questions.topic: Community Health Nursing as a Profession
questions.question_text: A Community Health Nurse identifies an increase in diarrhoeal disease cases in several households. Which professional action is most appropriate?

choices.text: Keep the information private and take no action
Document and report the suspected increase through appropriate surveillance channels and support relevant public health action
Wait until the disease affects every household
Announce the names of affected individuals publicly

questions.rationale: Community Health Nurses contribute to disease surveillance and the early identification of public health threats. Appropriate reporting supports timely investigation and prevention while protecting individual confidentiality.

questions.topic: Health Care Delivery System in Ghana and CHPS
questions.question_text: A client asks whether an active NHIS membership means that every medicine and service will be provided without restriction. What should the Community Health Nurse explain?

choices.text: NHIS covers every possible treatment and medicine without exception
NHIS provides access to services within its approved benefits package and applicable conditions
NHIS is only available to people working in government institutions
NHIS membership removes the need for clinical assessment

questions.rationale: The National Health Insurance Scheme provides financial protection for covered healthcare services under its approved benefits package. Membership does not mean that every medicine, procedure or service is automatically covered.

questions.topic: Patient Rights and Advocacy
questions.question_text: A nurse is providing health education to a group of adults with different literacy levels. Which approach is most appropriate?

choices.text: Use complex medical terminology to demonstrate professional knowledge
Use clear language, practical examples and teach-back to assess understanding
Provide information only to the most educated participant
Avoid questions because they may delay the session

questions.rationale: Health information should be communicated in a way that the intended audience can understand and use. Simple language, demonstrations and teach-back help identify misunderstandings and improve health literacy.

questions.topic: Legal Issues in Community Nursing
questions.question_text: A nurse is caring for an unconscious adult who requires immediate life-saving intervention, and no authorized representative is available. What is the most appropriate approach?

choices.text: Delay all emergency care until a relative arrives
Provide necessary emergency care in the client's best interests under applicable law and clinical protocols
Assume that the client has refused all treatment
Ask a neighbour to provide legal consent without authority

questions.rationale: In a genuine emergency, a delay in necessary treatment may cause serious harm. Care should be provided according to applicable emergency, consent and best-interests principles while the appropriate people are contacted when feasible.

questions.topic: Professional Ethics and Code of Conduct
questions.question_text: A nurse notices that a colleague has falsified a client's temperature record. What should the nurse do?

choices.text: Ignore the falsification to protect the colleague
Ensure the client's safety, preserve accurate information and report the concern through the appropriate supervisory process
Alter other records to make the entries consistent
Discuss the incident with unrelated community members

questions.rationale: Falsifying clinical records undermines patient safety, continuity of care and professional accountability. The concern should be reported through appropriate channels, and the clinical record must remain accurate and traceable.

questions.topic: History of Community Health Nursing in Ghana
questions.question_text: A CHPS zone has low attendance at child welfare clinics despite the availability of services. Which approach best reflects the community-participation principle underlying CHPS?

choices.text: Close the clinic because residents are not attending
Engage caregivers and community leaders to identify barriers and develop acceptable ways to improve attendance
Blame parents for failing to understand healthcare
Restrict services to children from households near the compound

questions.rationale: CHPS emphasizes community engagement and shared responsibility for improving health. Identifying local barriers with residents can help develop practical interventions that improve access and service utilization.

questions.topic: Professional Ethics and Code of Conduct
questions.question_text: A nurse working in a small community is approached by a local chief who requests the names of residents diagnosed with tuberculosis. What should the nurse do?

choices.text: Provide the names because the chief is an important community leader
Explain confidentiality obligations and share only information that is authorized or legally required for appropriate public health action
Post the names publicly to encourage treatment
Refuse all communication with the chief about tuberculosis prevention

questions.rationale: A client's diagnosis is confidential and should not be disclosed simply because a community leader requests it. The nurse may support public health action through authorized channels while limiting disclosure to what is necessary and legally permitted.

questions.topic: N&MC Regulations and Scope of Practice
questions.question_text: A Community Health Nurse is working in a resource-limited CHPS compound when a client presents with a condition requiring specialist management. The nurse has the basic skills to provide initial care but not definitive treatment. What is the best course of action?

choices.text: Attempt definitive treatment to avoid using referral services
Provide appropriate initial care within competence, arrange timely referral and communicate with the receiving facility
Discharge the client because specialist services are unavailable locally
Ask a volunteer to manage the condition independently

questions.rationale: Professional accountability requires the nurse to recognize the limits of local resources and personal competence. Appropriate initial management and timely referral help prevent avoidable deterioration while maintaining continuity of care.

questions.topic: Legal Issues in Community Nursing
questions.question_text: A nurse leaves a client with severe hypoglycaemia unattended after recognizing the condition, and the client subsequently sustains serious harm. Which legal concern is most directly raised?

choices.text: Breach of confidentiality
Possible negligence through failure to provide reasonable care
Appropriate delegation
Professional development

questions.rationale: A nurse has a duty to respond appropriately to a recognized clinical emergency within their competence. Failure to take reasonable action may constitute a breach of the standard of care, particularly where it contributes to harm.

questions.topic: Patient Rights and Advocacy
questions.question_text: A competent adult woman refuses a proposed referral to a district hospital despite being informed that her condition may deteriorate. Her family demands that the nurse force her to go. What should the nurse do?

choices.text: Force the woman into a vehicle because the family has requested it
Reassess her understanding and decision-making capacity, explain the risks and alternatives, document her decision and seek appropriate senior guidance
Discharge her without further discussion or documentation
Allow the family to sign a form overriding her decision

questions.rationale: A competent adult generally retains the right to refuse recommended care or referral after receiving relevant information. The nurse should ensure that the decision is informed and voluntary, document the discussion and follow applicable procedures.

questions.topic: Professional Boundaries
questions.question_text: A nurse regularly borrows money from a vulnerable client and threatens to withhold home visits if repayment is delayed. Which professional concern is most significant?

choices.text: Appropriate therapeutic relationship
Exploitation and serious breach of professional boundaries
Effective community mobilization
Acceptable professional delegation

questions.rationale: The nurse is using professional authority and the client's vulnerability for personal financial benefit. Such conduct is exploitative, undermines trust and may constitute serious professional misconduct.

questions.topic: Communication and Documentation Standards
questions.question_text: A nurse discovers that a colleague has documented that a child received a vaccine, but the immunization register and caregiver's account indicate that the vaccine was not administered. What should the nurse do FIRST?

choices.text: Accept the documentation because the colleague is senior
Verify the facts, protect the accuracy of the child's immunization record and report the discrepancy through the appropriate process
Administer every vaccine again without checking the child's immunization history
Delete the original entry without preserving an audit trail

questions.rationale: Inaccurate immunization records may result in missed or unnecessary doses and compromise public health data. The nurse should verify the facts, correct records according to policy and report suspected falsification or documentation errors.

questions.topic: Health Care Delivery System in Ghana and CHPS
questions.question_text: A CHPS zone records an increase in maternal complications, but the nurse's routine reports show very few antenatal contacts. Community discussions reveal that many pregnant women do not know that the CHPS compound provides maternal health services. What should the nurse prioritize?

choices.text: Assume that pregnant women are deliberately avoiding healthcare
Investigate access and awareness barriers with the community, strengthen health education and improve appropriate maternal service linkages
Stop recording antenatal contacts until attendance improves
Refer every pregnant woman directly to a teaching hospital

questions.rationale: The discrepancy suggests that limited awareness or access may be contributing to low service utilization. Community assessment and engagement can identify barriers and guide appropriate health promotion and referral arrangements.

questions.topic: Professional Ethics and Code of Conduct
questions.question_text: A nurse receives an instruction from a supervisor to record a health education session that never took place because the district requires a higher activity report. What should the nurse do?

choices.text: Record the session because the instruction came from a supervisor
Refuse to falsify the record, explain the concern and report the matter through appropriate channels
Record the session but leave the attendance list blank
Ask a community volunteer to sign the false report

questions.rationale: Professional accountability requires accurate reporting, even when a superior requests otherwise. Falsifying service data compromises public health planning and may constitute professional misconduct or a legal offence.

questions.topic: Legal Issues in Community Nursing
questions.question_text: A nurse is assessing an adult client who appears confused and is unable to understand the explanation of a proposed non-emergency procedure. A relative insists that the procedure should proceed immediately. What is the most appropriate action?

choices.text: Proceed solely because the relative has requested it
Pause the non-emergency procedure, assess decision-making capacity and follow applicable consent or lawful representative procedures
Assume that confusion permanently removes the client's right to make decisions
Ask another client to provide consent

questions.rationale: Decision-making capacity is specific to the decision and may fluctuate, so it should not be assumed absent merely because a client is confused. For non-emergency care, the nurse should establish the appropriate consent process before proceeding.

questions.topic: Patient Rights and Advocacy
questions.question_text: A client with a disability reports that clinic staff routinely discuss her condition with her caregiver instead of addressing her directly. What should the Community Health Nurse prioritize?

choices.text: Continue communicating only with the caregiver because it is faster
Advocate for accessible communication, address the client directly and involve the caregiver according to the client's wishes and applicable requirements
Exclude the client from all healthcare decisions
Advise the client to stop attending the clinic

questions.rationale: Disability does not automatically remove a person's right to participate in healthcare decisions. The nurse should promote accessible communication, respect the client's autonomy and involve support persons appropriately.

questions.topic: Health Care Delivery System in Ghana and CHPS
questions.question_text: A CHPS compound has limited supplies, and a nurse identifies several children with danger signs requiring urgent assessment. Which action should take priority?

choices.text: Complete routine administrative reports before attending to the children
Triage the children according to clinical urgency, provide appropriate immediate care and arrange urgent referral where indicated
Treat children in the order their caregivers arrived regardless of severity
Ask caregivers to decide which child should be treated first

questions.rationale: Clinical urgency, not arrival order, should guide prioritization when several clients require attention. Triage and timely referral help ensure that children with life-threatening conditions receive prompt care.

questions.topic: Professional Ethics and Code of Conduct
questions.question_text: A nurse learns that a colleague has been practising while visibly impaired by alcohol and is preparing to provide care to clients. What should the nurse do FIRST?

choices.text: Ignore the situation to protect the colleague's reputation
Protect clients from immediate risk by ensuring the colleague does not provide unsafe care and promptly notify the appropriate supervisor
Allow the colleague to continue if the clinic is busy
Post the colleague's condition on social media

questions.rationale: The immediate concern is the safety of clients who may receive care from an impaired practitioner. The nurse should take appropriate steps to prevent unsafe practice and report the concern through professional and institutional channels.
